## COURSE IN THE HOSPITAL:
Child was admitted with above mentioned complaints. Relevant Investigations were done. IV
fluids, IV antibiotics (Inj. Ceftriaxone) were started after taking sample for blood culture and
urine culture. As typhoid IgM ELISA was faintly positive, Syp Azithromycin was added. In view
of persistent fever spikes and usg showing grossly distended gall bladder antibiotics were,
escalated to Inj Piptaz and Amikacin on day 2 of hospitalization. Child was kept NPO for 24
hours on day 2 of hospitalization. Paediatric Surgeon,s opinion was obtained and advice were
carried out. BACTEC Blood culture showed Escherchia coli growth and sensitive to
Meropenem, so other antibiotics were stopped and Inj. Meropenem was given for 5 days Serial
USGs were done to monitor gall bladder size. Child improved clinically , afebrile for more than
medications 24 hours, , taking oral feeds well,no further episodes of vomiting ,hence being discharged on oral
PAEDIATRIC SURGEON'S OPINION(Dr. Senthil Ganesh): Diagnosed to have acalculous
cholecystitis advised NPO and escalation to Inj Piptaz
